summary: A leper kneels before Jesus and says, “If You are willing, You can make me clean.” Jesus touches him, cleanses him, and sends him to the priest.
key_insight: By the end of the story, Jesus and the leper have traded places. The man who had to live outside the towns goes about proclaiming, and Jesus “could no longer openly enter the city, but was outside in deserted places.”
story: While Jesus was in one of the towns of Galilee, a man full of leprosy saw Him. {Lk} He came and knelt before Jesus, {Mk} fell on his face and begged Him, {Lk} “Lord, if You are willing, You can make me clean.”
Jesus was moved with compassion. {Mk} He stretched out His hand and touched him, and said, “I am willing; be cleansed.” Immediately the leprosy left him, and he was cleansed.

Then Jesus strictly warned him and sent him away at once: {Mk} “See that you say nothing to anyone; but go your way, show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing those things which Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.” {Mk}

But the man went out and began to proclaim it freely and spread the news, so that Jesus could no longer openly enter a town. He stayed outside in deserted places, and people came to Him from every direction. {Mk} Great multitudes came together to hear Him and to be healed of their infirmities, and He often withdrew into the wilderness and prayed. {Lk}
differences: Matthew places the healing as Jesus came down from the mountain, after the Sermon on the Mount. Mark and Luke tell it earlier in their accounts, in “a certain city” (Luke), before the call of Levi.
Only Mark says Jesus was “moved with compassion” and that He strictly warned the man and sent him away at once.
Luke says the man was “full of leprosy.” The leper kneels (Mark), worships (Matthew) and falls on his face (Luke).
Only Mark tells that the man spread the news so that Jesus could no longer openly enter a town. Luke alone adds that Jesus often withdrew into the wilderness to pray.

scene.label: Leprosy
scene.text: The Bible’s word covers a range of serious skin diseases, not only what is now called leprosy. The Law required a leper to tear his clothes, cover his upper lip, cry “Unclean! Unclean!” and live alone outside the camp (Leviticus 13:45–46). He was cut off from family, worship and town.

scene.label: The touch
scene.text: Touching a person with such uncleanness made one unclean under the Law (Leviticus 5:3). Jesus often healed with a word alone. Here He reached out and touched the man first, and spoke after.

scene.label: Only God cleanses
scene.text: When Naaman came to be healed, the king of Israel tore his clothes and said, “Am I God, to kill and make alive?” (2 Kings 5:7). Apart from a sign given to Moses, the Old Testament tells of only two lepers healed: Miriam and Naaman.

scene.label: A testimony to them
scene.text: Leviticus 14 sets out what a healed leper must do: be examined by a priest outside the town, take part in a rite with two birds, wash, and on the eighth day bring offerings to the temple. A priest declaring him clean would be public proof of what Jesus had done.

witnesses.matthew: Places the leper first in the series of miracles that follows the Sermon on the Mount. In the Sermon, Jesus said He came not to destroy the Law but to fulfill it (Matthew 5:17); here He sends the cleansed man to keep it. The leper calls Him “Lord” and worships Him.
witnesses.mark: Tells the fullest story: Jesus’ compassion, His stern warning and the man’s disobedience. Mark alone shows what the healing cost Jesus, who was pushed out of the towns into deserted places.
witnesses.luke: Notes that the man was “full of leprosy,” an advanced case. Luke ends with Jesus slipping away to pray, a habit he mentions again and again (Luke 3:21; 6:12; 9:28).

seeing.reveals: Jesus is willing. The leper never doubted His power, only His willingness, and Jesus answered with a touch and a word: “I am willing; be cleansed.”
seeing.living: Many who trust that Jesus can still wonder whether He wants to, for someone like them. This man came with that very question and found compassion. Bring Jesus the thing that makes you feel untouchable; it did not drive Him back from this man.
seeing.ponder: Do you believe Jesus is able to make you clean, and do you believe He is willing?

preaching.big_idea: Jesus is not only able to cleanse; He is willing.
outline: A plea that doubts His willingness (40)
A command that honors the Law (43–44)
preaching.watch_for: The man’s question is about willingness, not power. Jesus answers in the man’s own words: “If You are willing” becomes “I am willing.”
